Tyler Christopher Herro was born on January 20, 2000.
Tyler Herro is an American professional basketball player.
Tyler Herro plays for the Miami Heat of the National Basketball Association (NBA).
Tyler Herro played college basketball for one year with the Kentucky Wildcats.
Herro was selected by the Miami Heat in the first round of the 2019 NBA draft with the 13th overall pick.
Herro was named to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team in 2020.
During his rookie season, Herro reached the NBA Finals.
In 2022, Herro was named the NBA Sixth Man of the Year.
Herro can play both point guard and shooting guard positions.
Herro was born in Greenfield.
Herro graduated from Whitnall High School in Greenfield, Wisconsin.
During his senior season at high school, Herro was named to the First Team All-State.
In his senior season, Herro averaged 32.9 points per game.
In his senior season, Herro averaged 7.4 rebounds per game.
In his senior season, Herro averaged 3.6 assists per game.
In his senior season, Herro averaged 3.3 steals per game.
Herro's field goal percentage was over 50 in high school.
Herro's three-point shooting percentage was 43.5 in high school.
Herro scored more than 2,000 points during his high school career.
Herro received scholarship offers from the University of Wisconsin–Madison, Marquette University, DePaul University, Oregon State University, and Arizona State University.
Herro committed to play for the University of Wisconsin after visiting the Madison campus many times.
Herro de-committed from Wisconsin on October 17, 2017.
When Herro was no longer committed to play for Wisconsin, he was recruited by the University of Kansas and University of Kentucky.
Calipari offered Herro a scholarship on October 31, 2017.
Herro visited the Kentucky campus and decided to play for Kentucky.
Herro signed his letter of intent with Kentucky on November 14, 2017.
Herro averaged 14.0 points per game as the only player to start in all 37 games for the Kentucky Wildcats.
On February 27, 2019, Herro scored a collegiate career-high 29 points against Arkansas Razorbacks.
Herro was named an All-Freshman First Team selection by Basketball Times.
Herro was named the Southeastern Conference Rookie of the Year by the Associated Press.
On April 12, 2019, Herro declared for the 2019 NBA draft and forgave his final three years of college eligibility.
Herro was selected by the Miami Heat with the 13th overall pick in the 2019 NBA draft on June 20, 2019.
On July 10, the Miami Heat signed Herro.
On October 23, 2019, Herro made his NBA debut and started against the Memphis Grizzlies.
In his NBA debut, Herro scored 14 points with 8 rebounds, 2 steals, and an assist.
Herro's career-high in points was 29 on October 29, 2019, against the Atlanta Hawks.
On August 12, 2020, Herro scored a career-high 30 points against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

When the Miami Heat defeated the Milwaukee Bucks in the second round of the 2020 NBA playoffs on September 8, 2020, Herro became the first player born in the 2000s to appear in an NBA Conference Finals game.
On September 15, 2020, Herro was named to the 2019–20 NBA All-Rookie Second Team by the league.
In game 4 of the 2020 Eastern Conference Finals, Herro scored a career-high 37 points against the Boston Celtics.
Herro set Conference Finals records for the youngest player (at 20 years, 247 days old) to score 30-plus points and the most points by a rookie.
After an Eastern Conference Finals victory against the Boston Celtics, Herro became the first player born in the 2000s to play in an NBA Finals.
During game 2 of the 2020 NBA Finals, Herro started at age 20 years, 256 days—eight days younger than Magic Johnson was when he started game 1 for the Lakers in 1980 against the Philadelphia 76ers.
In game 4 of the same Finals series, Herro achieved the most three-pointers made by a rookie in NBA playoffs history with 45 threes.

On October 9, 2020, Herro broke a 44-year-old record by scoring 10 points on the third quarter of game 5 of the 2020 NBA Finals—setting the NBA record for the most consecutive games in the playoffs scoring in double digits with 20 while surpassing Alvan Adams's record of 19 games.
The Miami Heat lost the series in 6 games to the Los Angeles Lakers in the 2020 NBA Finals.
On January 12, 2021, Herro scored a season-high 34 points against the Philadelphia 76ers.
On February 17, 2021, Herro grabbed a career-high-tying 15 rebounds against the Golden State Warriors.
On May 16, 2021, Herro logged a career-high 11 assists against the Detroit Pistons.
In the 2021 playoffs, the Miami Heat lost in four games to the Milwaukee Bucks in the first round.
On October 23, 2021, Herro became the first player in Heat franchise history to record at least 30 points and 10 rebounds off the bench against the Indiana Pacers.
On April 5, 2022, Herro scored a season-high 35 points against the Charlotte Hornets.
Herro was named the 2022 NBA Sixth Man of the Year, making him the first player in Heat franchise history to win the award.
During the first round of the playoffs, the Miami Heat eliminated the Atlanta Hawks in five games.
On May 2, 2022, Herro recorded 25 points and seven assists against the Philadelphia 76ers.
The Miami Heat defeated the Philadelphia 76ers in six games and advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals.
Herro missed games 3 through 6 of the series with a groin injury.
He returned for game 7 but only played seven minutes as the Heat were eliminated in a 96–100 loss.
On October 2, 2022, Herro signed a four-year, $130 million contract extension with the Miami Heat.
On November 2, 2022, Herro scored 26 points alongside a game-winning three against the Sacramento Kings.
On November 27, 2022, Herro recorded his first career triple-double with 11 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists against the Atlanta Hawks.
On December 15, 2022, Herro put up a career-high 41 points on 10-of-15 shooting from three-point range against the Houston Rockets.
He also became the youngest player in NBA history to put up at least 40 points, 10 three-pointers made, and five rebounds in a game.
On December 31, 2022, Herro put up a buzzer-beating, game-winning three-pointer against the Utah Jazz.
He finished the game with 29 points, nine rebounds, six assists, and two steals.
Herro ended the year as league leader in free-throw percentage at 93.4%.
Herro broke his right hand in the first round of the 2023 playoffs against the Milwaukee Bucks.
He was expected to be out for at least six weeks after undergoing surgery.
Even though he became available to play in game 5 of the NBA Finals against the Denver Nuggets, the Heat did not play him before losing the game and series to the Nuggets.
On October 30, 2023, Herro scored a season-high 35 points during a loss to the Milwaukee Bucks.
On April 24, 2024, in Game 2 of the First Round against the Boston Celtics, Herro put up 24 points, 5 rebounds, and a playoff career-high 14 assists.
Herro has two younger brothers named Austin and Myles.
Both of his younger brothers also play basketball.
His parents are Jennifer and Chris Herro.
He never learned how to swim.
Herro was included in the Jack Harlow song "Tyler Herro" named after himself, and features prominently in the music video.
In 2020, Herro began dating Katya Elise Henry.
On June 5, 2021, they announced that they were expecting a child together.
Their daughter was born on September 14, 2021.
On June 18, 2022, the couple announced that they were expecting their second child.
Their son was born on January 1, 2023.
